subject: `$_[N] =~ /\G…/` does not use the ARG BOX, so pos set through a defelem is invisible (pos.t t21)
description:
EXPOSED s361 by the prototype-arity fix (1279be6), which corrected the parse of `ok $_[3] =~ /\Ge/, 'desc'`. It is NOT a new bug — the row had been passing under a WRONG parse.

Before: `ok ($;$)`'s prototype made the site "strictly single", so the statement parsed as
    (ok($_[3])) =~ /\Ge/, 'desc'
and the emitted CL was `(p-=~ (pl-ok (p-scalar (p-aref-argbox @_ 3))) (p-regex …))` — the match ran on ok()'s RETURN VALUE, and the row scored "pass" for a reason unrelated to what it tests.
After: `(pl-ok (p-scalar (p-=~ (p-aref @_ 3) (p-regex "/\\Ge/"))) "…")` — which is what perl does.

With the correct parse the row fails, and the cause is visible in the same diff: the =~ target is `(p-aref @_ 3)` — a COPY — where the old (wrong) path happened to use `p-aref-argbox`, the defelem alias.  pos() lives on the box, so `pos $h{n} = 1` cannot be seen by a later `$_[3] =~ /\G…/` when the match reads a copy.

Family: this is the #131 defelem-aliasing family one step further along (there: writes to $_[0] lost; here: the match TARGET must be the alias box so pos/\G travel with it). Likely fix area: whatever decides argbox-vs-copy for a `$_[N]` used as a regex-bind target.

Baseline: the row `pos.t 21 \G works with defelem scalars` was added to docs/fail-baseline.tsv by EDIT in s361 with this cause, and docs/pass-baseline.tsv's pos.t row went 16/14 → 15/15.</description>
</invoke>
